name: TypeScript
summary: A statically checked, structurally and gradually typed superset of JavaScript from Microsoft whose types are erased at compile time; the compiler (tsc) type-checks and emits plain ECMAScript.
standards: ECMA-262 (runtime semantics of the JavaScript it erases to)

level_notes.0: Two official implementations: the original self-hosted compiler written in TypeScript (src/compiler on the release-6.0 branch of microsoft/TypeScript, the last JavaScript-based line) and the native Go port that became TypeScript 7 (microsoft/typescript-go). swc, esbuild, Babel and oxc only parse and strip types; they do not type-check.
level_notes.1: There is no maintained specification: the TypeScript Language Specification was last updated for TypeScript 1.8 (2016) and is archived in the repository. Current behaviour is defined by the compiler, per-release notes, the design goals/notes in the TypeScript wiki and, for runtime semantics, ECMA-262.
level_notes.2: The TypeScript Handbook is official but explanatory (it explicitly is not a specification), so it is filed at level 2.
level_notes.3: Rosetta Code reports 'blocked' to automated checkers.
